thread:
jia: Heads-up: I kicked off a preflight for the vnext release apply in us-east-1 (scheduled change window 23:00 UTC). Terraform plan shows a provider upgrade suggestion + a replace on an IAM role used by cross-account peering.
infra-bot: plan summary: 3 to add, 2 to change, 1 to replace (aws_iam_role.redwood-peering-role). Possible drift detected on module/networking/route-handlers. Full plan: https://ci.internal/plan/1734567890 :warning:
sam: can you paste the relevant plan snippet for the IAM role replace? worried about downtime for the peering handshake.
jia: ```diff
- resource "aws_iam_role" "redwood-peering-role" {
-   assume_role_policy = jsonencode({ ...old policy... })
- }
+ resource "aws_iam_role" "redwood-peering-role" {
+   assume_role_policy = jsonencode({ ...new sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity... })
+ }
```
anya: if that role is replaced it will invalidate the existing STS sessions right? that's risky during a rollover. we should avoid replace in a canary apply. :thinking_face:
leo: +1 to holding the replace. we can plan a targeted change: apply everything except the iam module, or use `-target=` for safe rollout.
deploybot: scheduled apply job queued at 1734570000 (23:00 UTC). Command: `deploybot apply --workspace=prod --plan-id=1734567890`. Auto-rollback disabled by default.
sam: hold apply. let's not run the global apply until we confirm a fallback. can we pin provider to previous minor and re-run plan? that might remove the replace.
jia: I already re-ran a quick plan with provider pinned to 4.0.3 and the IAM replacement disappears. New plan shows only non-critical route table updates. https://ci.internal/plan/1734567901
infra-bot: note: provider pin added at modules/provider.tf line ~12 in branch `release/vnext-pin`. diff available.
anya: proposal: run a canary apply in us-east-2 (lower traffic) with `-target=module.networking.route-handlers` and `-target=module.egress` to validate changes. keep IAM module excluded.
leo: also add a release note entry and an operational rollback playbook link in the canary run message. if anything fails, we want automatic branch rollback and a tfstate restore checklist.
sam: ok. decision: CANCEL global apply. schedule two steps: 1) canary apply in us-east-2 at 23:10 UTC excluding iam. 2) once canary passes, merge `release/vnext-pin` (provider pin), then run full apply in maintenance window with a 15m manual holdpoint.
ja'signal: accepted. I'll update the deploybot job to `apply --workspace=prod --plan-id=1734567901 --targets=module.networking,module.egress --exclude=module.iam` and set `--holdpoint=15m` after canary.
deploybot: update applied to queue. Canary job id: 1734567920. Will post summary when complete.
infra-bot: added rollback playbook link: https://confluence.redwood/infra/rollback-playbook and pinned runbook snippet in the job.
sam: also add a guard in the deploy pipeline to reject plans with `replace` for any `aws_iam_role` unless explicitly approved by security.
anya: yes please — I'll open a quick PR to the pipeline rules.
leo: small ops note: someone on-call should watch peering BGP state during the canary (ping checks + connection metrics). I'll volunteer to watch 23:00–00:00 UTC.
ja: thanks @leo. tagging @infra-oncall for visibility.
infra-oncall: acknowledged. I'll monitor escalation channel and be ready to trigger the escape hatch.
sam: escape hatch procedure in short: `deploybot abort <job-id>` then `terraform state pull > before.json` and run state restore from snapshot in s3 (see playbook). Keep communications in #incidents if we have any customer-facing impact. :white_check_mark:
jia: I'll post a short release note blurb after canary success and update the PR description with the pinned provider rationale.
deploybot: canary job 1734567920 started. logs: https://ci.internal/job/1734567920/logs
infra-bot: reminder: tag the change with `redwood-release/vnext` so billing and telemetry attribute properly.
ja: will do. moving to canary hold — I will update this thread with pass/fail within the next 30m. :rocket:
